# INFRA-555 plan: Dispatch's server signs people in, starts and reports health correctly at more than one pod

Spec: dispatch://INFRA-555/spec (version 1). Root: dispatch://INFRA-63/spec (version 25). Evidence: dispatch://INFRA-63/artifact/ha-audit-md, "Server core" F1-F3, F9, F10 and "Background" F6, F11. Code read at sjawhar/legion main aa64baf6; paths below are under `packages/envoy` unless they start with `packages/`.

## Decisions taken outside the spec (2026-10-27)

- INFRA-63 architect, 02:15Z, over Envoy: (1) INFRA-555 changes both sides of the `server.started` contract in one pull request; that pull request's review is the agreement. (2) The outbox's `scheduleRetry` pod clock (audit Background F11, `internal/dispatch/outbox/publisher.go:369-383`) goes to dispatch://INFRA-514; this plan does not touch the outbox. (3) Include a fix so a Google outage cannot sign people out (membership refresh, task 7). (4) Leave the `Importer` doc comment (`architecture/importer.go`, audit F10) to dispatch://INFRA-562 and the comment at `infra/gcp/dispatch_kube.go:391` (and the same claim at `infra/gcp/dispatch_test.go:851-853`) to dispatch://INFRA-560: those children replace that code. (5) The browser sign-in spec waits for dispatch://INFRA-559's two-process harness on `main`.
- With the INFRA-559 planner, 02:13Z-02:26Z: INFRA-559 builds the browser suite's two-process mode (`DISPATCH_E2E_PROCESSES=2`, round-robin proxy, `X-Dispatch-E2E-Process` pin honoured on every request kind); INFRA-555 adds `DISPATCH_E2E_SIGNIN=oidc` to it. INFRA-555 builds the one registry of live server processes (task 3), which INFRA-559 reads for its "new version" banner. INFRA-559's `DISPATCH_DEV_SIGNIN_SHARED_KEY` yields a key set of one value through task 1's type. Whoever merges second rebases.

## Design

### 1. Signing key set (spec item 2)

- `DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY` holds one or more keys separated by whitespace, parsed as `DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN` is (`auth/agent_token.go:73-109` `ParseSharedAgentTokens`: trim, split at each Unicode space, refuse an empty or repeated entry naming its position and never its value). The first key signs new cookies and seals refresh tokens; every key verifies a cookie and opens a seal. Reuse that parser's splitting and refusal code rather than writing a second one.
- A new `auth.SigningKeys` value (current key plus accepted keys) replaces the `string` key everywhere it travels: `sessionSigningKey` (`cmd/dispatch/main.go:808-821`), `openPeople` (`cmd/dispatch/signin.go:155`), `routes.AppContextOptions.SigningKey` (`routes/router.go:125,359`), `identity.CookieIdentity.SigningKey` (`identity/identity.go:24,35`), `store.NewPgPeopleStore` (`store/people.go:35`).
- `auth.VerifySession` (`auth/session.go:118-148`) accepts a cookie whose HMAC matches any key (constant-time compare per key). `IssueSessionCookie` signs with the current key.
- The refresh-token seal (`store/refresh_token_seal.go`) keeps the `v1:` format byte for byte: it seals under the current key's HKDF key and opens by trying each key's AEAD (the GCM tag rejects a wrong key). No key id. Reason: `RetirePlainRefreshTokens` (`store/people.go`) treats any value not `like 'v1:%'` as plain text and revokes it at the issuer, so a new prefix would make an older build that boots during a roll or a rollback revoke every new seal and sign those people out.
- No cookie re-issue code. A cookie verified under an older key stays valid until its own expiry (30 days, `auth/session.go` `sessionMaxAgeSeconds`); a seal opened under an older key is re-sealed under the current key by the next hourly confirmation (`ConfirmSubject`/`Confirm` already call `seal.seal`). The rotation procedure, written in `cmd/dispatch/README.md` and the docs site: (a) add the new key second and roll every process; (b) move it first and roll; (c) remove the old key no sooner than 30 days after (b). A release that ships the key set is never the release of a first rotation, and no build older than the key set is rolled back to while the setting holds two values (an older build reads `"K1 K0"` as one key).
- A single value that contains whitespace changes meaning (it becomes two keys). Production's key is a 64-character alphanumeric password (`infra/gcp/dispatch_cloud.go:127`), so it is unchanged; the CHANGELOG says a hand-written key with inner whitespace signs people out once.
- `auth.SigningKeys.Fingerprints()` returns hex of the first 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(key, "dispatch signing key fingerprint v1") for each key, current first. Used only by task 3's boot check; a fingerprint reveals nothing of the key.

### 2. Sign-in state in a signed cookie (spec item 1, audit F1)

- `authStart` (`routes/router.go:249-271`) stops writing `pendingStates`. It sets `dispatch_oauth_state` to `s1.<b64url JSON {state, nonce, next, exp}>.<hex HMAC>`, signed under a key derived from the current signing key for this purpose alone (HKDF or HMAC with the label "dispatch oauth state v1"), so a state cookie never verifies as a `dsession` cookie or the reverse. Cookie attributes unchanged (`oauthStateCookieFor`: `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure` unless insecure, `SameSite=Lax`, `MaxAge` 600).
- `authCallback` (`router.go:279-326`) clears the cookie first (as now), verifies the cookie under every accepted key, refuses a cookie whose `exp` has passed, requires the URL's `state` to equal the cookie's `state` (constant time), takes `nonce` and `next` from it, and answers the existing 400 "invalid or expired state — start over at /auth/start" on any failure. `next` is sanitised again at the callback (`sanitizeNext`) and capped at 1024 bytes at the start (longer falls back to `/`) so the cookie stays far below a browser's 4 KiB limit.
- Removed: `pendingMu`, `pendingStates`, `pendingState`, `putPendingState`, `takePendingState`, `maxPendingStates`, the 429 "too many pending sign-in attempts" answer and their tests (`router_test.go` `TestAuthStartCapsPendingStates`, `TestOAuthCallbackRejectsExpiredPendingState`, `TestAuthStartEvictsExpiredPendingStates`).
- Single use: the map deleted an entry on use; the cookie is cleared on the callback, Google's authorization code is single-use, and `Exchange` requires the ID token's nonce (`oidc/codeflow.go:127`). Written in the router's comment.
- A sign-in that starts on a pre-change build and ends on a post-change build fails once (the person starts again). Accepted: production runs one server pod with `Recreate` at one replica (`infra/gcp/dispatch.go:30-33`) when this release ships (root item 7), so no two builds serve a sign-in at once. Told to INFRA-558, whose two-build test must not sign in across a pre-INFRA-555 build.

### 3. Registry of live server processes, and the no-key refusal (spec item 2 last sentence; shared with INFRA-559)

- Migration `0121_server_processes.up.sql` (+ `.census.sql`, `select 0` with a comment; renumber at rebase if a sibling lands a 0121 first): table `server_processes` (`instance uuid primary key`, `commit text not null default ''`, `dashboard_build text not null default ''`, `signing_keys text[] not null default '{}'`, `started_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `heartbeat_at timestamptz not null default now()`), and table `server_build_announcements` (`seq bigint generated always as identity primary key`, `commit text not null`, `announced_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `published_at timestamptz`). Add-only, so the earlier build reads and writes the schema unchanged (README "Database migrations" rule).
- New package `internal/dispatch/processes`:
  - `Register(ctx, pool, Instance{Commit, DashboardBuild, SigningKeys})`: in one transaction under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (a new fixed key), read the live rows (`heartbeat_at > now() - 15 s`), refuse with `ErrKeySetMismatch` when a live row's current fingerprint is not in this process's fingerprints or this process's current fingerprint is not in that row's `signing_keys`, else insert. The error names the other instance and says to give every process the same `DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY` (rotation: add the new key second first). The lock serialises two processes booting at once, so the second sees the first.
  - Heartbeat every 5 s (`update ... set heartbeat_at = now()`); `Deregister` deletes the row; `Live(ctx)` returns rows within 15 s of the database's `now()`; a prune loop under `duty.Exclusive` (lease `server-processes`) deletes rows older than 10 minutes.
  - `DashboardBuild` is hex of the first 16 bytes of sha256(`<web dist>/index.html`), the bytes `servePage` already hashes for its ETag; `''` when there is no web dist. Whichever of INFRA-555 and INFRA-559 lands first defines this function; the other reuses it.
- `main` (`cmd/dispatch/main.go`): after `net.Listen` (:462) and before serving, run one database probe, then `Register`; a refusal logs the error and exits 1 before any request is served. Deregister after `serveUntilStopped`'s HTTP drain has ended (`cmd/dispatch/shutdown.go`), so a draining pod counts as live until its last request is answered. Operator subcommands (`runSubcommand`) never register.
- This is how "a process started with no key refuses to start in a multi-process deployment" is met: a process that minted its own key in its data dir (`auth.LoadOrCreateSigningKey`) has a fingerprint no peer holds, so it refuses when any other process is live, and a peer refuses to start beside it; processes that share one data dir share the file's key and start. The same check refuses a pod that boots with a changed secret beside pods holding only the old key, which would otherwise sign people out (root "What the code assumes", "A changed secret reaches each pod only when it happens to restart"): the roll stalls with an error naming the rotation steps while the old pods keep serving. Dev sign-in needs no exemption: it is loopback-only and one process unless INFRA-559's shared key is set.

### 4. `server.started` once per fleet-wide build (spec item 5, audit F9 / Background F6)

- Contract (subject and payload unchanged, so the daemon's durable filter `consume.go:88-134`, its NATS grant `nats_permissions_test.go:78` and the strict TS schema `packages/contracts/src/dispatch-api.ts:1881` still fit): `notifications.dispatch.server.started`, `source: dispatch`, payload `{commit, started_at}`; meaning "every live Dispatch server process serves `commit`", published once each time that fleet-wide commit changes; `started_at` is the database's time of the announcement. Event id, source event id and dedupe key: `dispatch-server-started-<commit>-<seq>`, where `seq` is the announcement row's.
- `internal/dispatch/startup` replaces `PublishStarted` (per-process, before listen, `startup/started.go:59-96`, `main.go:447`) with `Run(ctx, Deps{Pool, Publisher, Leases, Clock})` started after `Register`: every 5 s, under `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` (another fixed key), read `Live`; when every live row has the same non-empty `commit` and the latest announcement names another commit (or none), insert an announcement; then publish every announcement whose `published_at` is null with `PublishReportingDuplicate`, and set `published_at` on acknowledgement. A process whose NATS is down leaves the row unpublished, and any process publishes it once its bus answers. A restart of every pod on one commit announces nothing; a rollback from C2 to C1 announces C1 again with a new `seq`.
- `/healthz` gains `fleet_commit`: the latest announcement's commit, `null` when none. The daemon's `BuildCommit` (`packages/daemon/internal/dispatch/client.go:243-260`) returns `fleet_commit` when the body carries the field (`""` when it is null) and `commit` when it does not (a Dispatch older than this change). Reason: the daemon boot's `dispatch build` wake (`daemon/workflow.go:589-608`) reads `/healthz` through the Service, which mid-roll is any pod's answer (audit Background F6, third bullet). `commit` keeps its meaning (this process's build), which `legion/checks/dispatch-production-check.sh` reads.
- One-time transition: builds before this change do not register, so the first release that carries it announces as soon as its own pods agree, and an old pod restarted during that release still publishes its own start. Production runs one pod with `Recreate` for that release (root item 7), so no old pod serves beside it. Written in the README.
- Daemon side: `intake/decode.go` and `workflow/check.go` keep the persisted cause string `dispatch start` (`check.go:35`, exposed in `api/state.go:438` and `packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts:182`); the task text at `check.go:162` becomes "Dispatch serving build <sha> on every server process", and the comments of `serverStarted`, `buildShape`, `decodeServerStarted`, `ServerStarted` (`intake/facts.go:744`) and `BuildCommit` say the new meaning.
- One shared fixture, `packages/daemon/internal/intake/testdata/dispatch/server-started.json` (the envelope `startup` builds for commit `0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f00f1e2d3c`, seq 7, a fixed time), read by the Dispatch test (built envelope equals the fixture), the daemon intake test (decodes it to `ServerStarted{Commit}`), and `packages/contracts/src/dispatch-api.test.ts` (its payload parses under `DispatchServerStartedPayloadSchema`).

### 5. Start and serve without NATS (spec item 3)

- `internal/bus`: a connect option (for example `WithConnectInBackground()`) for `Connect`, `ConnectOwningStream` and `Dial`. Configuration errors stay fatal and are returned before any dial (bad nkey seed, `refuseRemoteNATS`, bad SOCKS5 setting). Unreachable servers do not fail the constructor: the client is returned without a live connection and connects in the background, retrying forever as nats.go's reconnect does. With the option: the owning client runs `ensureStreamWithConfig` on its first live connection (today only in `newClient`, `nats.go:260-267`; its body is INFRA-558's and is not edited here); `Subscribe`/`SubscribeCore` called before the first connection bind on it (today `Subscribe` reads `c.js` without `ensureConn`, `nats.go:289-300`); reconnect hooks run on the first connection; `Connected()` reports false until then; a publish waits within its own context and then fails as it does while reconnecting. `nats.RetryOnFailedConnect` with a connect handler is one way; the implementer chooses after reading `connectWithContext` and the recovery code. The listener and every other caller keep today's behaviour (they do not pass the option).
- An authorization refusal at connect is not fatal: the process serves, logs the refusal at ERROR at most once a minute, and `/healthz` reports `"nats": false`.
- `cmd/dispatch/main.go`: `ConnectOwningStream` (:182), the agent-stream `Dial` (:203) and `connectIntake` (:432-434) pass the option. `cmd/dispatch/redeliver.go` stops opening the KV bucket at boot (`redeliver.OpenState(natsClient.JS())`); the sweeper opens it on its first pass that finds NATS connected and retries on later passes (smallest change in `redeliver/`, since INFRA-562 changes `sweep.go`). The agent conversation route (`api/agent_stream.go`) must neither hang past its own timeout nor crash while NATS has not connected, and relays once it has; the test pins what it answers.
- `/healthz` (`main.go:972-1030`): status 200 when the database probe answers, 503 when it does not (unchanged); `ok` means "this process can serve requests" and no longer depends on NATS; `nats` still reports the connection (`null` when NATS is disabled). The e2e scripts' `jq -e '.ok and .nats'` (`scripts/e2e/dispatch-user-turns.sh:236`, `dispatch-session-settings.sh:213`) still wait for both. `/healthz` stays the readiness probe; the README says it is not a liveness check, because it fails while the database is unreachable (told to INFRA-560, which adds liveness probes).

### 6. Start without the sign-in issuer or the service-account issuer (spec item 4, audit F3)

- `internal/oidc`: `CodeFlow` (used only by Dispatch) discovers lazily: a constructor that reads nothing, a `Discover(ctx)` under single-flight with a 10 s attempt timeout and at least 5 s between failed attempts, and a background loop from boot that retries (1 s doubling to 30 s) and logs each failure at ERROR at most once a minute. Until discovered, `AuthURL` (now `AuthURL(ctx, …) (string, error)`), `Exchange`, `Refresh` and `Revoke` return an error matching `oidc.ErrIssuerUnavailable`. Remove `DiscoverCodeFlow` and anything else the change leaves unused.
- A lazy wrapper around `oidc.Verifier` for Dispatch's service-account tokens, with the same discovery rules; `cmd/broker` and `cmd/listener` keep `oidc.Discover`. `api.Deps.OIDC` and `routes.AppContextOptions.OIDC` take an interface so the verifier stays non-nil before discovery (`api/server.go:644` takes the token path only when it is non-nil).
- Answers before discovery: `/auth/start` and a callback whose exchange meets `ErrIssuerUnavailable` answer 503 `SIGNIN_UNAVAILABLE` ("the sign-in issuer cannot be reached; try again in a minute"); a JWT bearer answers 503 `OIDC_ISSUER_UNAVAILABLE`, never 401; shared and personal agent tokens are served as before.
- The people store's revoker (`openPeople`) is the lazy code flow, so `retirePlainRefreshTokens` and the per-sign-in retirement fail one token and retry at the next boot, as they do today when the pool does not answer.
- `/healthz` gains `signin` and `service_tokens`: `true` once discovered, `false` before, `null` when not configured. Neither decides the status; a deploy check that needs sign-in asserts `signin: true`.

### 7. A Google outage does not sign people out (architect decision 3)

- `CodeFlow.Refresh` classifies its failure: `oidc.ErrGrantRefused` when the token endpoint answered 400/401 with OAuth error `invalid_grant` (RFC 6749 section 5.2: the refresh token is expired, revoked or not the client's); every other failure (no answer, timeout, 5xx, 429, `invalid_client` or another code, a token response without a verifiable ID token, `ErrIssuerUnavailable`) matches `oidc.ErrIssuerUnavailable`.
- `identity.Membership.refresh` (`identity/membership.go:84-86`) ends the sign-in only on `ErrGrantRefused` and on the rule checks after a successful refresh (unchanged). On `ErrIssuerUnavailable` it returns the error: the request is refused (fail closed: no one is served on a lapsed confirmation), the session generation and the refresh token are kept, and the next request after the issuer answers refreshes. Every caller of `identity.Identity.Login` (API `writeAuthenticationError` at `api/server.go:718-724`, the document and delivery websockets, the page routes) answers it 503 `SIGNIN_UNAVAILABLE` rather than 500.
- `oidctest.Issuer` gains a token-endpoint failure control (status and OAuth error), beside `RevokeGrants` and `FailRevocation`.

### 8. Database clock for time-gated writes (spec item 6, audit Background F11 outside the outbox)

- `confirmed_at`: `WriteSignIn` (`routes/router.go:313`) and `WriteConfirm` (`identity/membership.go:99`, rules in `identity/domain_rule.go`, `group_rule.go`, `person.go:61-67`) stop taking a Go time; the people store writes `now()`. `PgPeopleStore.Membership` returns the confirmation's age as the database measures it (`now() - confirmed_at`), and `Membership.fresh` compares that age with `MembershipMaxAge`; `Membership.Now` goes.
- `delivery/store.go:122-128` `RecordEventAt`: `greatest(coalesce(last_event_at, now()), now())` with no time argument (caller `delivery/intake.go:682`).
- `delivery/deployed.go:112-115`: `deployed_event_at = now()`; `RecordDeployedEvents` loses its time parameter (callers `delivery/intake.go:218` and `delivery/reconcile.go:169`; only `is null` is ever read). So `delivery/intake.go` changes in exactly two places, the arguments at :218 and :682, and nowhere else.
- `delivery/changes.go:88-89` `PruneChanges`: `delete from delivery_changes where at < now() - $1::interval` with `ChangeRetention` (caller `reconcile.go:184`).
- Checked and left: the session cookie's expiry and the state cookie's `exp` are signed with one pod's clock and checked with another's; they gate no write, and seconds of skew against 30 days and 10 minutes change nothing.

### 10. Browser sign-in across two processes (root acceptance, two-build line)

A code-flow issuer a browser can sign in at, as a command: `packages/envoy/cmd/dev-oidc-issuer` today serves only service-account tokens (`--token`, `cmd/dev-oidc-issuer/main.go:1-15`); the code flow exists only in `oidctest.Issuer` (`EnableCodeFlow` `issuer.go:194`, `SignInAs` `:260`), driven from Go in the same process. Extend the command (it already serves `oidctest.New` on loopback and publishes one key): `--code-flow <client id>=<client secret file>` arms `EnableCodeFlow` with its published key; `--sign-in-as <email>` sets the person every authorization signs in as when none is queued (the claims Dispatch's domain rule reads: `sub`, `email`, `email_verified`, `hd` from the email's domain); and a loopback-only `POST <issuer URL>/_dev/sign-in-as` with a JSON claims body queues the next person (oidctest `SignInAs`), so a spec chooses who signs in. The command logs `issuer listening url=<URL>` as now. A test in `cmd/dev-oidc-issuer` drives one authorization and token exchange through the flags and the control route.

After INFRA-559's two-process harness is on `main`: add `DISPATCH_E2E_SIGNIN=oidc` to it (`packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh` builds each server's environment from `DISPATCH_E2E_*` inputs; `harness-listeners.ts` gains one row that runs `dev-oidc-issuer --code-flow dispatch-e2e=<secret file> --sign-in-as <the harness's person>` and reads its URL from the `issuer listening` line): both servers get `DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER` (that URL), `DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID` `dispatch-e2e`, `DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET` (the same secret) and `DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN` (the person's domain), one shared `DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY`, one `DISPATCH_SERVER_URL` (the proxy), and no dev sign-in. New spec `packages/dispatch/e2e/signin.multiprocess.e2e.ts`: pin `/auth/start` to process A and, with `page.route` adding `X-Dispatch-E2E-Process: b` to the `/auth/callback` navigation, the callback to B; assert the person lands on `next` signed in, and that a request pinned to A and one pinned to B both answer as that person.

## Risks

- Moving the stream ensure to first connect: a listener and a Dispatch of different builds already rewrite the stream at each boot (audit F8, INFRA-558); this change adds no new writer.
- `RetryOnFailedConnect`-style clients and the client's own recovery (`recovery.go`) can both dial; the implementer must keep the invariant in `ensureConnWithContext`'s comment (only one live connection per client). The `internal/bus` race tests (`race_test.go`, `-race`) must stay green.
- Registry heartbeats ride the shared pool; if they fail for 15 s a live process looks gone and the announcement can go out while it still serves an old build. Heartbeats use a short timeout and log failures; acceptable for a wake that a production check confirms itself.
- Migration number collision with siblings: renumber at rebase.
